about: The words BEAM Campfire uses again and again, for the translators to settle first so both the web wallet and the desktop/phone app use the same ones. Fill ru, zh-Hans and ja for each term, then translate the catalogs (src/i18n/<lang>.json) with these words. 'meaning' says what the term is; 'where' names screens where it appears.
keep_as_is: bETH and the other asset tickers
addresses, transaction IDs, amounts, BEAM names, dApp and publisher names

terms.meaning: The app's account on this device: the coins, addresses and history that one set of 12 words (or one wallet.db file) controls. Several can live on one device.
terms.where: Welcome, Home (its name), Settings → Wallets, Unlock

terms.meaning: The recovery phrase: twelve English words that rebuild the wallet on any device. The words themselves are never translated (BEAM accepts only its English list); everything said about them is.
terms.where: Backup, Check your words, Restore, Settings → Backup

terms.meaning: Keeping the 12 words (or the wallet.db file and its password) somewhere safe, away from this device.
terms.where: Settings → Backup, Home's backup reminder, Welcome

terms.meaning: Rebuilding a wallet from its 12 words on this device.
Bringing in an existing wallet.db file made by another BEAM wallet (it keeps its own password).
terms.where: Welcome, Import a wallet.db, Add a wallet

terms.meaning: Saving a copy of this wallet's wallet.db file, protected by a password, to open in another BEAM wallet.
The wallet's database file as BEAM's desktop and command-line wallets use it. 'wallet.db' itself is a file name: keep it as is.
What unlocks the wallet on this device (and every payment). Not the 12 words; it cannot recover the wallet elsewhere.
terms.where: Set a password, Unlock, Change password, every payment

terms.meaning: A key kept by the device behind Face ID / Touch ID / the device PIN, used instead of typing the password. 'Face ID' and 'Touch ID' are Apple's names: keep them.
terms.where: Face ID setup, Settings → Face ID / Touch ID, Unlock

terms.meaning: Opening the wallet with the password or Face ID after it locked.
Closing the wallet so nobody can use it without the password; 'Lock now' does it at once.
Locking by itself after some minutes without use (1, 5 or 15 min), also when the app goes to the background.
terms.where: Settings → Auto-lock, Unlock ('Locked after 5 minutes without use')

terms.meaning: Where someone sends BEAM to this wallet: a long code to copy, share or show as a QR code. Never translate an address itself.
terms.where: Receive, Send, Settings → Your addresses, Contacts

terms.meaning: The usual BEAM address: the receiver's wallet has to come online within about 12 hours to accept a payment.
terms.where: Receive → More, Send review, Your addresses

terms.meaning: An address that receives even while the receiving wallet is closed; payments to it cost a higher network fee.
An address whose payments hide among many others; the receiver can spend them after a while; higher network fee.
A reusable donation address that receives while its owner is offline; higher network fee.
Getting BEAM or a token into this wallet: the screen that shows the address and its QR code.
terms.where: Home, Receive, Activity's empty state, many 'Receive BEAM first' hints

terms.meaning: Paying someone: amount, address, network fee, then confirm.
One transfer in or out of the wallet, as listed in Activity.
How much is sent or received. Amounts are written with a dot for decimals in every language (1,234.5) and are never translated.
What the wallet holds of an asset; 'available' is what can be spent now.
The part of the balance that can be spent now (not still arriving, sending or maturing).
Coins the wallet received or made that the network does not let it spend yet (they become available after some blocks).
What the BEAM network charges for a payment or a contract call (0.001 BEAM for a regular payment, more for others). Paid to the network, not to the app.
terms.where: Send, Review, Swap, every approve sheet

terms.meaning: The button that fills in the whole available amount minus the network fee.
The screen that shows exactly what will happen (amount, fee, address) before the person confirms.
terms.where: Send → Review, Swap, Move coins, Ethereum send

terms.meaning: The final 'yes' to a payment or action, after the review.
A regular payment sent while the receiver's wallet was offline: it completes when that wallet comes online (within about 12 hours).
A payment being built or registered on the network.
A payment the network has accepted, waiting to be in enough blocks.
A payment stopped before it was sent; nothing left the wallet.
A payment that did not go through; the wallet says why.
The list of payments, swaps and contract calls of this wallet (its history).
A code the sender can give to show a payment was made to an address; the receiver can check it.
terms.where: Payment details, Settings → Check a payment proof

terms.meaning: The identifier of one payment on the network (a long hex code, never translated).
A private note the person attaches to a payment or an address, kept only in this wallet.
A person the wallet owner pays, saved with a name and address.
A name the person gives an address (to remember what it is for).
The square code that holds an address or a payment request, shown on Receive and read by Scan.
Reading a QR code with the camera (an address, a payment request, a BEAM name).
Putting a text (an address, a key) on the clipboard; 'Copied' confirms it.
Where copied text waits to be pasted; the app empties it after a minute when it held a secret.
The separate pieces the wallet's balance is made of (like notes in a purse); several coins let several payments go at once.
Dividing a large coin into several smaller ones so several payments can be sent at the same time.
Coins held in BEAM's most private form (max privacy / shielded), spendable after a while.
Bringing the wallet up to date with the BEAM network. 'Synced' means up to date and able to send.
terms.where: Home's status line, Activity, Send (paused until synced)

terms.meaning: Syncing: the wallet is behind the network by some blocks and is getting the rest.
How far the wallet is from the newest block (a count of blocks; plural forms).
One step of the BEAM blockchain, about one a minute; 'block 3,928,666' is a height.
A BEAM server the wallet talks to over the internet to see the blockchain and send payments.
The default: the app picks one of BEAM's public nodes and moves to another one by itself when it fails.
A BEAM node the person runs and enters by its address, used instead of random nodes.
terms.where: Settings → BEAM node → Your own node

terms.meaning: Moving to another node because the current one stopped answering; sending pauses for a moment.
What a node (or another server) can see: the device's IP address. Explained before the first connection.
terms.where: IP privacy notice, Settings → IP privacy

terms.meaning: Rebuilding the wallet's coins from the blockchain (from BEAM's recovery file) when the balance looks wrong; history and addresses stay.
terms.where: Settings → Rescan, Getting your wallet ready

terms.meaning: BEAM's daily snapshot of the blockchain (~330 MB) that a restored wallet reads to find its coins quickly.
terms.where: Restore, Getting your wallet ready, Rescan

terms.meaning: A key that lets a BEAM node see every payment this wallet receives (for one's own node). A secret: never share it.
terms.where: Backup → Show owner key, BEAM node, Your own node

terms.meaning: A newer signed release of the app; it installs only when the person taps Update.
terms.where: Settings → Check for updates, Home's update banner, About

terms.meaning: The release key's proof that an update or file comes from BEAM Campfire and was not changed.
One version of the app (all its files, signed together).
Another web address serving the same signed releases, asked for updates when this app's own address is gone.
terms.where: Check for updates, Update from another address, About

terms.meaning: The small part of the app the browser installs first; it checks every file against the signature before the app runs.
terms.where: Install (first open), update messages, the tripwire

terms.meaning: Code at the app's address that BEAM Campfire did not sign: the app stops and tells the person not to enter a password.
Where an installed web app sits on the phone, like any app (iPhone: Add to Home Screen).
The release number, e.g. 'Version 0.2.14'.
Any coin the BEAM wallet holds: BEAM itself or a Confidential Asset (token). Asset names and tickers are never translated.
terms.where: Home, Send, Swap, a token's page

terms.meaning: A Confidential Asset on BEAM (or an ERC-20 on Ethereum): anything other than BEAM itself.
terms.where: Home, Hidden tokens, Your own token

terms.meaning: Tokens the person chose not to see on Home; they stay in the wallet.
terms.where: Settings → Hidden tokens, a token's page

terms.meaning: What an amount is worth in the person's currency (from CoinGecko, only once allowed).
Exchanging one asset for another at the DEX's current price (BEAM > bETH by default).
The most the price may move against the person before a swap is refused ('slippage tolerance' in trading jargon: do not use that word).
How much of one asset one unit of the other buys (1 BEAM = … bETH).
A pair of assets locked in the DEX that swaps trade against; people add to it to earn fees.
The assets someone puts into a pool (adding) or takes out of it (withdrawing).
The token a pool gives for added liquidity; it is what takes the liquidity out again.
BEAM's on-chain exchange (a contract), where swaps and pools live.
Asking a BEAM smart contract (DEX, names, airdrop…) to do something; it costs at least 0.011 BEAM.
The sheet where the person checks what a contract call or a dApp request will spend and says yes or no.
An app that runs inside the wallet and uses BEAM contracts (the wallet asks before it spends anything).
BEAM's catalogue of dApps from their publishers, to install from.
Who made and signed a dApp in the DApp Store (their names are never translated).
A Confidential Asset the person creates (the minter): its name, symbol and supply.
terms.where: Home → Your own token, Create a token, Mint

terms.meaning: Making more units of one's own token.
How many units of a token exist (or may exist: the limit).
terms.where: Your own token, a token's page

terms.meaning: Destroying an amount of a token for good.
A readable name (like a username) that points to a BEAM address; names are never translated.
terms.where: BEAM names, Send, Receive a name

terms.meaning: Taking into the wallet what waits for it (payments to a name, an airdrop code, a vault).
Where payments to a BEAM name wait until the owner claims them.
Paying to keep a BEAM name for another period before it expires.
Sending amounts to many people at once as codes they redeem.
One airdrop voucher: a short text that claims an amount once (plural forms).
One set of airdrop codes created together.
The second wallet in the app, for ETH and Ethereum tokens (WBEAM…), made from its own 12 words.
What the Ethereum network charges (paid in ETH); the Ethereum word for network fee.
terms.where: Ethereum send, Swap on Uniswap, Move coins

terms.meaning: Taking BEAM or an asset across to Ethereum and back (BEAM's bridge).
Getting BEAM with another coin through an exchange service, sent to this wallet.
The address of the exchange service where the person sends their other coin for a buy or a swap.
A message from the app on the device (a payment arrived, a reminder), made on the device, never from a server.
How the app looks: theme, colours and language.
Light or dark (or like this device).
The language of the app's words (like this device, or English, Русский, 简体中文, 日本語 — each written in itself).
The default for theme and language: follow what the phone or computer is set to.
Removing this wallet from this device only; the coins stay on the blockchain and come back with the 12 words.
terms.where: Settings → Delete wallet from this device

terms.meaning: The app runs in one browser tab or window at a time; another one has it now.
